To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we report the first isolation of two NMD-1 positive strains, Raoultella planicola and Escherechia coli, from a patient, and that the bla NDM- 1 was carried by two plasmids that were found to be able transfer the NDM- 5 gene in vitro.
we have isolated a new NDM-1 carrying plasmid, which is a composite of an ISCR1 and a bla NDM- 1, which can self excise to form a free circular form and can be transferred to other plasmids.
we isolated two strains of E. coli and Raoultella sp. that harbored the same bla NDM- 1 element, which is a novel ISCR1 element.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of the novel NDM-1 gene in the clinical environment and the potential of its dissemination.
the emergence and spread of NDM1-mediated carbapenem-resistant bacteria and their clinical significance.
the isolation of two strains bearing a novel ISCR1 element carrying bla NDM- 1 and their in vitro transferability in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patient was colonized by NDM-1 producers during hospitalization.
bla NDM- 1 was acquired by R. planticolo and E. coli in the patient, and the bla NDM-5 was acquired by R.pplanticolo from E.coli in the patient.

bla NDM-2 was found to be carried by a 58 kb IncI2 plasmid in E. coli and a 280 kb IncF plasmid in R. plantcida, and bla NDM-4 was carried by a novel 58 kb IncFIIA plasmid pNDM-4-1 in E. coli, and bla NMD-5 by a 280 plasmid pNMD-5-1 in R.pantica
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a novel NDM-1 carrying ISCR1 element could be self-excisable and transferrable.
the NDM- 1 positive Raouletta planticola was the primary source of bla NDM1, and bla NDM1 was transferred from the Raouletta plasmid to the E. coli plasmid via a free form of the ISCR1 element.
the NDM- 1 positive E. coli and R. planticole isolated from the patient were probably derived from an ancestral strain carrying a 58 kb NDM-1-positive plasmid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated that the NDM- 1 gene is capable of being transferred between bacteria in vivo, which is of great concern for public health.
NDM-1 is not limited to the Enterobacteriaceae, but can be carried by other Gram-negative bacteria.
the NDM- 1 gene was transferred between two different species in the patient.
